name: Swiss plastic pop watch
summary: A cheap Swiss quartz watch in a plastic case with a bright pattern. The maker sells it as an accessory and changes it each season. The Swatch line of 1983 set it.

philosophy.core_thesis: A watch can be a fashion accessory that one wears for a season. The maker sells colour and a pattern at a price that allows many watches.
design_principles: Mould the case from plastic in one piece with the strap lugs, so that it needs few parts.
Limit the number of parts to about 51, with a quartz module that the maker welds into the case.
Print a bold pattern in two to four colours on the dial, the strap or the case.
Release two collections each year, so that the buyer returns each season.
Make the dial large and flat with simple hands, so that the time is clear.
Make the strap from the same plastic as the case, in a vivid colour.
Price each watch at the level of a pair of shoes, so that one can own many.
Invite artists and designers to draw the face for limited editions.
anti_patterns: A leather strap with a classic buckle
A plain grey dial with no colour
A complex movement that one cannot repair cheaply
A dial with fine print and small numerals
A watch that costs as much as a suit

silhouette.shape: A thin round plastic case with a flat glass, a one-piece strap and a bold printed dial.
silhouette.line: A flat disc with a smooth side, a plain bezel and a strap that clips straight into the case.
silhouette.fit: The strap is soft and light, and the case lies flat on the wrist.
silhouette.proportion: Case thickness to width about 1 to 4; the dial fills about 80 per cent of the face; the strap is 17 mm wide.
rules: Make the dial a flat field for graphics, with hands that stay clear of the print.
Use bright primary and neon colours on the case, the strap and the dial together.
Keep the case a single colour and print the pattern on the dial only.
Use bold simple numerals or no numerals at all.

fabrics.rule: Use moulded plastic for the case and for the strap, a flat plastic crystal for the glass, and print the pattern on the dial.

methods: plastic crystal fixed in the case
construction.closures: A plastic or steel buckle closes the strap; the crown sits flush with the case.
construction.details: A bright dial pattern, a one-piece strap in a vivid colour, a flat case and a clear plastic crystal.

surface.pattern: Geometric shapes, stripes and dots in bright colours on the dial and the strap.
surface.gloss: Matt plastic at 15 to 35 GU; glossy plastic at 70 to 90 GU; the crystal at 85 GU.
surface.wear: The plastic scratches and fades in the sun; the strap yellows and cracks; one replaces the watch, not the part.

palette.strategy: Bright primary and neon colours in blocks, with white and black for the hands and the print.

processes: injection moulding of case and strap
making.scale: Mass production in millions of watches a year, with new designs twice a year.
making.signs: A moulded plastic case, a bright pattern on the dial and a one-piece strap.

pieces.form: One-piece plastic strap in a vivid colour
Soft strap with a printed pattern
Thin plastic case with a printed dial
Flat clear crystal over a bold dial
Fabric strap with a plain steel buckle

emotion.target_response: Playful delight: the viewer sees a cheap, loud toy that tells the time and goes with any outfit.

use_cases: a prop for a film set in the 1980s
an image prompt for a stack of plastic watches
avoid_when: the brief wants luxury or craft
the brief wants steel or gold
the brief wants a rugged tool watch

modifiers.how: Swap plastic for steel and gold, cut a patterned dial and make a bracelet from the case line.
Replace the dial with a touch screen and keep the plain strap and the soft colours.
